subject: Pricing MAP: sensitivity scenarios & prefetch/batching test plan
messages:
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@medivance.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.chhoi@redwood.com>
Cc: Medivance Procurement <procurement@medivance.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Request: MAP with cost assumptions and test plan

Irene — thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement wants a draft Mutual Action Plan that includes the evaluation schedule and the explicit cost/unit assumptions we'll use for scoring the PoC. Two asks to include in the MAP so we can move to procurement review: 

- Clear tokens/$ assumptions (tokens per request + expected response tokens) across the three model tiers we discussed.
- Expected savings from prefix caching and prefetching (if applicable) and how that changes tokens/$ during the PoC.
- Batching assumptions for inference (max batch size, expected latency impact at target throughput).
- A short timeline with milestones for eval, procurement review, and legal sign-off — target close by the end of Jan if possible.

Can you attach a draft MAP with those sections and a spreadsheet we can circulate to finance? Procurement would prefer a single-sheet cost sensitivity matrix they can review.

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: Request: MAP with cost assumptions and test plan

Alex — thanks, this is exactly what we should capture. I attached a first-pass MAP and a one-page token-econ summary (medivance_map_draft_v1.xlsx / token-econ-scenarios.pdf). Highlights below and a proposed schedule: 

- What you'll find in the draft MAP: objectives, acceptance criteria for the eval (latency, accuracy baseline, throughput), cost sensitivity matrix, and a short procurement checklist.
- Cost assumptions are presented as 3 scenarios (Baseline / Optimistic caching / Aggressive batching). Each scenario shows tokens per interaction, tokens/$ at our hosted price, and estimated monthly cost at target QPS.
- Prefetch/prefix caching: we capture a conservative 22% token reduction in the PoC baseline, with an optimistic 40% case after warm-up. Details and sample latency traces are in the CSV.
- Batching: recommended PoC batch sizes are 1 (latency-focused), 4 (balanced), 12 (throughput-focused). We call out latency deltas at each.

Proposed timeline (high level):
- Week 1 (Dec 6–10): Sign MAP, kickoff PoC infra (we'll provide test harness).
- Weeks 2–4 (Dec 13–Jan 7): Evaluation + iterative tuning (caching, batch tuning, quantization trials).
- Week 5 (Jan 10–14): Finish eval, deliver cost sensitivity sheet to your finance team.
- Week 6 (Jan 17–21): Procurement/legal review and sign-off.

Internal note: looping in Vanessa and Rishi to validate the tokens/$ math and confirm the batch-latency numbers. Vanessa — can you drop the quick sensitivity numbers inline so Alex and procurement have a single-sheet view? Rishi — any constraints we should call out around quantized model variants affecting token accounting?

Thanks — attaching files.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Manager, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Dec 2, 2026 at 9:20 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Internal note: looping in Vanessa and Rishi to validate the tokens/$ math and confirm the batch-latency numbers.

Thanks — quick sensitivity snapshot below (I pulled numbers into the attached CSV: prefetch-batch-latency-sample.csv).

Assumptions for PoC (example request profile):
- Input tokens per req: 75 (avg user prompt)
- Output tokens per resp: 220 (avg assistant response)
- Round-trip tokens per call (no caching): 295
- Hosted price used for scenarios: $0.0004 per token (example list price for the selected model tier in the MAP)

Scenario math (monthly projection at 5M requests):
- Baseline (no caching, batch size=1): tokens/month = 5M * 295 = 1.475B tokens => cost = $590k
- Prefetch conservative (22% token reduction): tokens/month = 1.149B => cost = $459.6k
- Aggressive caching + batching (40% token reduction + effective batching factor = 3): tokens/month effective = (1.475B * 0.6) / 3 = 295M => cost = $118k

Latency notes (measured from sample traces):
- batch=1: p95 = 210ms
- batch=4: p95 = 260ms (+50ms)
- batch=12: p95 = 420ms (+210ms)

Questions for procurement/finance: what risk tolerance for optimistic caching should we show? I modeled both conservative and optimistic so the team has guardrails.

Attachment stubs: prefetch-batch-latency-sample.csv (latency by batch size), token-econ-scenarios.pdf (single-page matrix).

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Carter <alex.carter@medivance.com>, Medivance Procurement <procurement@medivance.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: MAP with cost assumptions and test plan

Vanessa / team — a couple of operational caveats to make sure the MAP is actionable:

1) Model variants & quantization impact:
- We recommend testing both the full-precision tier and a 4-bit quantized variant during the PoC. Quantized model reduces token compute cost but may slightly affect latency and occasionally output quality; include a small acceptance tolerance in the eval (e.g., <=1.5% metric drop on your NLU pass).

2) Effective tokens accounting when using prefix caching:
- Our runtime charges per output token generated, but caching reduces input tokens sent upstream in many cases (prefix cached locally). For clarity in the MAP we show total remote tokens (billed) vs local tokens cached (not billed). The numbers Vanessa reported assume remote tokens after caching.

3) Batching interplay with latency SLOs:
- If Medivance needs strict p95 < 250ms, plan the PoC to keep batch size <=4 for the latency-run. If throughput testing is the objective, increase batching but gate on p95 and tail latencies in the MAP acceptance criteria.

Quick recommended production profile for the MAP (concise):
- Eval phase: run both variants for 2 weeks each, measurement windows of 24 hours after warm-up.
- Cost sensitivity: include three lines in the spreadsheet — remote_tokens (billed), local_cache_savings (tokens saved), and effective_billing_tokens.

Inline micro-table (expected token/$ at $0.0004):
- Full-precision (no caching): tokens/call 295 => cost/call = $0.118
- Full-precision (22% cache): tokens/call 230 => cost/call = $0.092
- Quantized (22% cache): tokens/call 230 => cost/call = $0.092 * (quantized compute adj 0.75) = $0.069

I'll add short rows to the attached XLSX for these variants. Also flagging that network egress and private deployment options may shift the final vendor pricing line items if Medivance opts for Dedicated or Private during procurement.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal, Applied ML / Inference Optimization
Redwood Inference
